title: The Unexpected Deadline
preview_description: Your manager needs an urgent compliance report today, but your schedule is already full. Practise raising the deadline conflict, agreeing what can move, and keeping the review step.
attribution: Original fictional scenario for practice. The dialogue and consequences are predefined and are not official organisational policy.
learning_goals: Raise capacity and deadline concerns early and respectfully.
Agree priorities without skipping required review steps.

characters.name: Alex
characters.personality: Under pressure but open to practical options

nodes.speaker: C2
nodes.narration: Your manager needs an urgent compliance report for the VP by the end of the day. Your schedule is already full, and the report needs a careful review. What do you say?

choices.text: “Sure, I'll drop everything else and get it done today.”
choices.reply: “Thanks for jumping in. Before you drop everything, let's check what's already due. I don't want us to create a second problem.”
choices.consequence: You were cooperative, but committed before checking the trade-offs or review time. Confirm priorities and protect the steps needed to complete the report accurately.

choices.text: “I can't. I'm too busy with my current deadlines.”
choices.reply: “I understand you're busy, but I need more than a no. Bring me an option so we can decide what moves.”
choices.consequence: Setting a boundary is reasonable, but a flat refusal gives no path to resolve the urgent request. Explain the conflict respectfully and suggest a concrete next step.

choices.text: “I can help. My current deadlines are A and B; which should move so I can finish this accurately and keep the review step?”
choices.reply: “That's fair. Let's move the vendor review to tomorrow and keep the client deadline in place. Thanks for raising the trade-off early.”
choices.consequence: You made your capacity visible, asked your manager to agree the priority trade-off, and kept the review step in view instead of silently cutting corners.

endings.title: Check the trade-offs before committing
endings.summary: You accepted the urgent report before checking the work already due.
endings.feedback: Cooperation helps, but an immediate commitment can hide capacity and review risks. Confirm what should move before promising a deadline.

reflection.prompt: What should you check before accepting an urgent deadline?

options.text: Agree which existing task moves and preserve the necessary review.
Promise to finish everything, then skip review if time runs short.

endings.title: Pair a boundary with a next step
endings.summary: You named that you were busy but did not offer a way to resolve the conflict.
endings.feedback: A respectful conversation can make the deadline and workload visible, then agree what changes. Suggesting a trade-off makes the concern actionable.

reflection.prompt: How can you make a capacity concern actionable?

options.text: Explain the conflict and ask which current priority should move.
End the conversation with a flat refusal.

endings.title: Make the priorities visible
endings.summary: You raised the capacity conflict and agreed a practical trade-off with Alex.
endings.feedback: You communicated early and respectfully, clarified which deadline would move, and kept the review step in the plan.

options.text: It surfaced capacity, agreed priorities, and kept the review step.
It promised every task would be finished without changing anything.
